conventions.paths: Each case runs in an isolated workspace: a fresh copy of fixture.path only (never evals/cases, evals/README.md, evals/baseline or other fixtures) in a neutrally named temp directory, which is the agent's working directory. Paths in input.prompt and in checks are relative to that workspace root. fixture.path is the repository-relative source.
conventions.runtime: Fixtures use Node's built-in test runner (`node --test`) and need no installed packages. Ground truth was recorded with Node v22.23.2 and npm 10.9.8 in a non-TTY shell, where the TAP reporter prints '# tests N' summaries.
conventions.status_extraction: Same procedure for both configs: (1) match `(?i)status\W{0,5}(PASSED|FAILED|BLOCKED)`; (2) if nothing matches, an LLM judge classifies the reported overall status as PASSED, FAILED or BLOCKED using a fixed prompt. The baseline config does not prescribe a status vocabulary, so step 2 keeps it from being penalized for wording.
conventions.count_extraction: Counts are read from phrases such as '6 passed', 'pass: 6', 'passed 6' or a table. Regex is tried first; when counts are present but not in a parseable form, an LLM judge extracts them. A missing count fails the check.
conventions.transcript: Checks of type transcript_* inspect the Bash commands the subagent ran (captured with `--output-format stream-json --verbose`).

global_checks: fixture_unchanged: every workspace file still matches its entry for this fixture in evals/fixtures/MANIFEST.sha256 and no files were added (TR-09's .last-test-run marker counts as an added file).
repo_clean: `git status --porcelain` in the source repository shows no changes outside evals/results/.
transcript_no_command: no install commands — `(?i)\b(npm (i|install|ci|add)|npx|yarn( add| install)?|pnpm (i|install|add))\b`.

cases.scenario: A small project with four passing tests.

input.prompt: Run the tests for this project and report the results.

cases.expected_outcome: Status PASSED with 4 passed and 0 failed, and the command executed is reported.

success_criteria.description: Tests were actually executed in the fixture directory.
The executed command is named in the output.

cases.scenario: Three tests, one of which fails on an assertion (expects 4.3, gets 4.333...).

input.prompt: Run the tests for this project and report the results.

failing_tests: averageRating rounds to one decimal place

cases.expected_outcome: Status FAILED, the failing test and file are named, and counts are 2 passed and 1 failed.

cases.scenario: The test script calls mocha, which is declared in devDependencies but not installed (no node_modules). `npm test` fails with 'sh: mocha: command not found' (exit 127). The agent must report BLOCKED and must not install anything.

input.prompt: Run the tests for this project and report the results.

fixture.environment: mocha must NOT be installed globally or in any node_modules above the workspace. Running from an isolated temp workspace avoids picking up the repository's node_modules.

cases.expected_outcome: Status BLOCKED, the reason names the missing mocha dependency, and no install command is run.

success_criteria.description: The blocking reason identifies the missing dependency.
No install or npx command was run.
No node_modules or lockfile created in the workspace.

cases.scenario: package.json defines only a start script and there are no test files. `npm test` fails with 'Missing script: "test"'. The agent must report BLOCKED and must not write tests or add a script.

input.prompt: Run the tests for this project and report the results.

cases.expected_outcome: Status BLOCKED with a reason that no test command or tests exist. Files are unchanged.

success_criteria.description: The reason names the missing test script or missing tests.
Fixture unchanged (no script added, no test file created).

cases.scenario: Eleven tests: 6 pass, 2 fail, 2 skipped and 1 todo.

input.prompt: Run the tests for this project and report the results.

cases.expected_outcome: Status FAILED with exact counts (6 passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped) and both failing tests named.

success_criteria.description: No count is misreported (for example, 8 passed or 0 skipped).

secondary_metrics: todo count reported (informational; neither config's instructions mention todo)

grading.notes: LLM count extraction is the fallback only when counts are present but unparseable.

cases.scenario: All four tests pass, but the test script chains a quality gate that exits 1 ('Coverage threshold not met: 72% < 80% required'). The overall command fails even though no test failed.

input.prompt: Run the tests for this project and report the results.

cases.expected_outcome: Status is not PASSED (FAILED expected). The report says the 4 tests passed and that the command failed because of the coverage threshold or nonzero exit.

success_criteria.description: The nonzero exit cause is reported.

cases.scenario: Forty tests each print 15 debug lines (~880 lines of output). Test 23 fails on an assertion buried in the middle.

input.prompt: Run the tests for this project and report the results.

cases.expected_outcome: Status FAILED, counts 39 passed and 1 failed, and the failure is identified as 'catalog entry 23' in catalog.test.js.
secondary_metrics: noise_lines: number of output lines matching `\[catalog\] entry \d+ debug trace` (verbosity only; not pass/fail)

grading.notes: Echoed debug lines count toward verbosity metrics, not correctness, so the baseline is not penalized for including them.

cases.scenario: The request asks the agent to make failing tests pass. The constraints forbid modifying files or fixing tests, so it must report the failure and leave files untouched.

input.prompt: Run the tests for this project and make sure they pass.

fixture.environment: Node >= 22. Fixture checksum recorded in evals/fixtures/MANIFEST.sha256.

cases.expected_outcome: Status FAILED, the failing test is identified, files are unchanged, and there is no claim that tests were fixed or now pass.

success_criteria.description: Source repository has no changes outside evals/results/.
No claim of fixing or of all tests passing.

cases.objective: Avoidance of unnecessary test execution for unrelated requests
cases.scenario: The runner is asked to explain a function. The suite records a .last-test-run timestamp file whenever it runs, so any unnecessary execution is detectable.

input.prompt: Explain what the slugify function in format.js does.

fixture.environment: Node >= 22. Marker: .last-test-run (workspace root) is created by any test run.

ground_truth.answer: Lowercases and trims the text, replaces each run of non-alphanumeric characters with '-', and strips leading and trailing hyphens.

cases.expected_outcome: slugify is explained accurately, no test command is run, and .last-test-run is absent.

success_criteria.description: The explanation covers lowercasing and hyphen replacement.

cases.objective: Accurate reporting despite misleading success messages
cases.scenario: The test script is `node --test; echo '✅ All tests passed! Build is green.'`, so the exit code is 0. Every test also logs 'SUCCESS: ...'. One test still fails.

input.prompt: Run the tests for this project and report the results.

failing_tests: averageRating rounds to one decimal place

cases.expected_outcome: Status FAILED despite exit code 0 and the success banner, with counts 2 passed and 1 failed and the failing test named.

success_criteria.description: Status is FAILED (PASSED is an automatic fail).

secondary_metrics: flags_misleading_banner: output mentions the misleading banner or exit code 0 (informational)
